written.myAnswer: The water surface is 20 m + 2 m = 22 m above ground level. Therefore, P = ρgh = (1000 kg m⁻³)(10 m s⁻²)(22 m) = 2.2 × 10⁵ Pa.
Liquid pressure increases as depth increases; it is directly proportional to depth.
The pressures are equal, because both points are at the same depth in water.
An increase in pressure at one part of a confined liquid is transmitted equally throughout the liquid. Hydraulic brakes use this principle.
Liquid pressure depends on the liquid’s density, the depth, and gravitational field strength. It is calculated using P = ρgh.
